conservation.condition_narrative:
1. The painting was removed from the stretcher and the reverse was vacuum cleaned. 
2. It was lined with a heavy linen and a wax resin adhesive. 
3. Grime was removed with swabs dampened in distilled water, followed by petroleum benzine. 
4. Some varnish was left, since the yellows were soluble. 
5. The painting was stretched on a new stretcher. 
6. It was sprayed with n-butyl-isobutyl-methacrylate-copolymer resin. 
7. Inpainting was done with dry pigments ground in methacrylate. 
8. It was sprayed again with the same resin as above. 
9. Heavy cardboard was placed on the reverse for protection. Metal strips were screwed to the stretcher to prevent the frame from abrading the paint film.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Frances Lehman Loeb Art Center in 2025.

conservation.condition_narrative:
Consolidation: 
Insecure paint around the small punctures was consolidated using Beva 371 (a proprietary adhesive based on ethylene vinyl acetate, approximately 15% in petroleum benzine). 
Surface Cleaning: 
Accumulated grime was removed from the paint surface using a solution of 0.02% Triton X-100 (non-ionic surfactant) in deionized water, cleared with deionized water. Any residual cleaning material was cleared with petroleum benzine. 
Correction of Planar Deformations: 
The deformations from the punctures in the canvas were returned to plane with gentle heat and pressure from the reverse. 
Revarnishing & Compensation: 
Losses in the punctured areas were isolated with B-72 (ethyl methacrylic methyl acrylate copolymer, 10% in xylene), and filled with Dap vinyl spackle. Paint losses were compensated using Bocour Magna Colors, pigments ground in acrylic resin, and gloss adjusted with Soluvar matte varnish (acrylic resins, 10% in xylene) and B-72. 
Frame & Refitting: 
The original backing board was returned to the painting. The painting was refitted into the frame using the original hardware. New D-ring hangers were attached to the reverse of both vertical members

credit_line: Bequest of Mrs. Arthur Schwab (Edna Bryner, class of 1907)
description: In this semi-abstract composition, a thin green line runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right of the canvas. On the right side of the line, a brown tree with clusters of green foliage rises from the bottom of the canvas. Behind the tree is a softly shaded background in tones of green, pink, white, and gray. To the right of the green line are two rounded, pink forms and a large, arching green shape surrounding them.
title: Spring
